text.p: Advance Bank Australia Ltd managing director John Thame said on Tuesday that banks in future require rational pricing where charges levied on transactions started to reflect the cost of deliver.

Thame told a Securities Insititute of Australia briefing that the current situation where lower income earners did not pay fees for five transactions saw banks performing a social security function for the government.
"Banks quite clearly can not continue down that track," he said.
"In future we are going to have to see rational pricing, which means the charges levied on transactions, will have to start to reflect the cost of deliver modes," he said.
Thame later told reporters banks had to face a social responsilbility, but this was not being shared by the new non-bank competitors.
The issue was currently not an issue in discussions between financial insititutions and the government, but it should be put on the agenda, he said.
